analysis:
Examined docs/reference/configuration.md head lines 354-687. The only changed line is head line 414, which documents the new DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED environment variable. That variable selects the Gated DeltaNet prefill kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35 models. Documented behavior: the default probe keeps the four-row kernel only where it reproduces gated_delta_step bit-for-bit on the GPU. Forced packed/rows kernels skip that check and are documented as A/B-only. The variable is read once per process and is not forwarded to LaunchAgents.

Threat-model fit:
- T-007/T-012/T-027 (output manipulation): the provider operator (ADV-001) already controls the local environment and weights, so an operator-forced kernel adds no new trust boundary.
- T-056 (attestation overclaim): attestation does not claim correct computation.
- A-001 confidentiality and the T-041 prefix-cache bindings: unaffected by a kernel choice.
- Daemon behavior: because the variable is not passthrough, installed daemons use the probe default.

The remaining text in both units is unchanged context, including the SSD cache, KEK and TTL rows relevant to T-041. Those rows are consistent with the threat model's descriptions (TTL ≤ 1800, kill switch, DEBUG-only key file).

The library implementation in libs/mlx-swift-lm GatedDelta.swift was not supplied. Its bit-exact probe claim and whether a probe mismatch fails safely cannot be verified from this evidence. That is a correctness and qualification question rather than a demonstrated security regression. No findings.
